Geometry | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Quadrilaterals and Polygons

Ride the Polygon Loop

How much do you turn on a full lap?

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 9–10
Topic
Interior and Exterior Angles
Standards
HSG-CO.C.10, HSG-MG.A.1, 8.G.A.5

Students derive the polygon interior angle sum (n − 2) · 180° by splitting polygons into triangles, discover the 360° exterior angle sum by “riding” a loop, and find the number of sides from an angle measure.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Find the interior angle sum of any polygon using (n − 2) · 180°.
  • Use the fact that the exterior angles of a convex polygon add to 360°.
  • Find a missing angle in a polygon.
  • Find the number of sides of a regular polygon from an angle.

3Essential question

Why does a rider always turn exactly 360° on one lap of any loop?

5MTB connection

Ride a lap of any loop trail or pump track and you turn through one full circle in total, however many corners there are. Each corner’s turn is an exterior angle; together they make 360°.

Pump-track designers use this: if a loop has five berms of equal turn, each berm turns 72°.

The mathOn the trail
Exterior angleHow far you turn at a berm
Exterior sum = 360°One full rotation per lap
Interior angleThe angle inside the loop at a corner
Regular polygon loopA loop with identical berms

7MTB activity

MTB Classroom Activity

Design a Pump-Track Loop

Use the 360° exterior angle sum and the interior angle sum to design a polygon-shaped pump-track loop.

You’ll need: Masking tape and a protractor (for the floor demo); Grid paper; Calculator
